A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GSE research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E. Content can be matched despite formatting changes and figure relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original attack-performance, runtime, explainability, transferability and ablation results in Section 3 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical evaluations in Section 3 and Appendix E, including the results in Tables 1–9.

M1.justification: The two-phase GSE procedure, proximal operator, spatial adjustment of regularization parameters, selected-coordinate projection and accelerated-gradient updates are unchanged in Section 2 and Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, ImageNet and NIPS2017, retaining targeted and untargeted attacks, adversarially trained classifiers and black-box transferability scenarios.

E2.justification: Figure 5's ImageNet/VGG19 comparison reports Sparse-RS instead of SAPF in v5, alongside the retained GSE, StrAttack, FWnucl and PGD0. Comparator membership in the other reported comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, target-label selection, classifiers, metrics, training settings and the 200-iteration attack budget are retained. Figure 5 still uses 1,000 ImageNet images, ten target labels and the same percentile sweep.

E4.justification: The adversarial-training comparison, transferability evaluation, k-hat ablation and qualitative case studies retain their designs and evidence. Figure 5 retains its existing percentile sweep; its revisions concern comparator and result attribution.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Averaging and best/average/worst-case reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 5 assigns v3's SAPF curve to PGD0 and v3's PGD0 curve to Sparse-RS. This changes method-specific reported results despite unchanged curve coordinates; it does not establish rerunning experiments. All numerical entries in Tables 1–9 match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, optimization formulations and Appendix C equivalence proof are retained. Correcting the missing subscript in the successful-example count and the omitted ASM argument harmonizes notation without changing the definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about group-wise sparsity, explainability, computation speed and attack success, including the 50.9% and 38.4% sparsity improvements.

C2.justification: Appendix E.3 expands the earlier claim of comparable transferability into claims about outperforming StrAttack below the diagonal, outperforming FWnucl on the diagonal and balancing within-model and cross-model performance. Table 8 is unchanged, and the StrAttack advantage is not uniform: one corresponding entry is 8.61% versus 8.72%.

D1.justification: Sections 3.1 and 3.3 and Appendix D.1 retain the same hardware, training schedule, attack hyperparameters, implementation descriptions and access information for code, image indices and target labels.

R1.justification: The acceleration sequence in Equation 14 is attributed to Beck and Teboulle (2009) in v3 and Nesterov (1983) in v5, with the corresponding bibliography replacement. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section hierarchy are retained. Changes include localized wording and notation corrections, the rewritten transferability paragraph, revised author/affiliation information and conversion to author-year citations.

P2.justification: The document-wide ICLR formatting changes the title and author block, typography, margins, headers, table styling and float placement. Algorithm 1 and Figure 2 relocate, Figures 3 and 4 exchange numbering/order, Figure 5 changes legend labels and markers, and stray x characters disappear from Table 7.

improvement.justification: v5 resolves Figure 5's inclusion of SAPF despite Section 3.4 stating that its ImageNet evaluation was excluded, fixes inconsistent notation and removes stray Table 7 characters. These provide limited clarity and consistency gains; the method, proof and all tabulated results remain unchanged. The more assertive transferability interpretation has mixed support in the unchanged Table 8, limiting the overall improvement.
